artists.biography: "Public Service Broadcasting"  are a London-based pseudonymous musical group consisting of J. Willgoose, Esq. on guitar, banjo, other stringed instruments, samplings and electronic musical instruments, Wrigglesworth on drums, piano and electronic musical instruments, and J F Abraham on flugelhorn, bass guitar, drums and assorted other instruments including a vibraslap. The band have toured internationally and in 2015 they were announced as nominees in the Vanguard breakthrough category of the fourth annual Progressive Music Awards, staged by Prog magazine, which they won.

perplexity.description:
The Last Flight is Public Service Broadcasting's fifth studio album, released in October 2024 on SO Recordings. The record continues the British electronic outfit's established practice of constructing concept albums around historical narratives, this time centering on aviator Amelia Earhart's final flight and disappearance in the Central Pacific. The album blends electronic instrumentation with post-rock sensibilities, featuring pulsing synths, interlocking percussive melodies, and experimental arrangements that convey both the technical precision and human drama of aviation history.

Musically, The Last Flight maintains the band's signature fusion of indie electronic and post-rock elements while exploring themes of danger, beauty, and human ambition. Rather than adopting a somber tone despite Earhart's tragic fate, the album emphasizes vitality and forward momentum, with tracks like "Electra" (named after Earhart's aircraft) showcasing energetic, pace-driven compositions. The production balances archival audio elements—a hallmark of Public Service Broadcasting's approach—with contemporary electronic textures, creating an immersive sonic narrative across its 39-minute runtime.

The album marked a significant moment in the band's career trajectory, arriving after their 2021 album Bright Magic had peaked at number two on the UK charts. The Last Flight debuted at number three on the UK Albums Chart, demonstrating sustained commercial interest in the band's work. The release was supported by an extensive European tour, with multiple UK venue dates selling out prior to the album's arrival, underscoring the band's growing audience and the continued appeal of their historically-informed, musically adventurous approach.
